title: Electrical Integration Systems Engineer, Edge Compute and Communications
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

OUR TEAM

Within Anduril, our team develops unmanned aerial systems capable of terminal guidance, long range intelligence collection, precision navigation, and unsupervised autonomy.  Anvil, Altius, Ghost, and other developmental UAS platforms operate in remote environments with limited user input, driving requirements for reliability and autonomy.  We have developed an autonomy stack that receives user intent, responds to detections processed at the edge, and coordinates flight patterns for groups of assets.  We want systems engineers with experience in this field to help design and manage the next generation of Anduril’s flight vehicles.  In order to succeed at Anduril, a systems engineer needs familiarity with simulation and rapid prototyping development to drive complex electro-mechanical and aero-performance design trades, in addition to supporting the engineering product development, production, and sustainment through the entire product lifecycle.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Lead development for an end-to-end solution by collaborating with cross-functional teams to define requirements and system architecture

• Design, develop, and maintain system components that meet functional and performance requirements in complex system environments

• Conduct thorough testing and debugging to ensure the reliability, scalability, and resilience of software applications, especially within a distributed systems context

• Work closely with hardware engineers and product managers to ensure seamless integration of software and hardware components

• Collaborate with the team to define and document software engineering processes and practices, ensuring adherence to quality standards and regulatory requirements

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• A passion for systems design, development, integration, and testing

• 2-6 years of industry experience including but not limited to electrical engineering, aerospace engineering or systems engineering

• Comfort with systems modeling tools such as Cameo

• Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodologies and the ability to operate effectively in an Agile development environment

• Hands-on prototyping, troubleshooting, and build experience of complex robotic systems

• Experience developing automated test scripts and frameworks using a common language (eg, Python, MATLAB, etc)

• Extremely organized and detail-oriented, and excellent verbal & written communication skills

• A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture

• Ability to obtain a U.S. security clearance

• Ability to travel domestically up to 25% as needed for test planning and execution, and excitement to work onsite at our headquarters in Costa Mesa, CA the rest of the time!

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Hands-on experience with prototyping, troubleshooting, and building complex robotic systems

• Familiarity with IP- based networks

• Experience with mission systems to include communications systems and components

• Familiarity with aviation airworthiness considerations

• Already hold a U.S. Secret security clearance, or higher

US Salary Range
$146,000 — $194,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary

title: GTM Compliance Analyst
description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

The Compliance team is responsible for ensuring Compliance at Plaid with all the laws and regulations that apply to us, as well as our internal policies. We help make sure Plaid stays within the bounds of our legal obligations, and partner with business stakeholders to build processes and systems to demonstrate our compliance.

Role Description

As a GTM Compliance Analyst, you’ll help Plaid evaluate and onboard customers in a way that supports growth while protecting the company from regulatory and compliance risk.

You’ll review prospective and existing customer deals, assess customer business models and use cases, conduct risk-based diligence, and determine when additional conditions, approvals, or escalations are needed.

You’ll work closely with Sales, Account Management, Legal, Product, and Customer Oversight to translate complex requirements into practical guidance and keep deals moving.

You’ll also help build the playbooks, workflows, and reporting needed to make GTM compliance more consistent and scalable as Plaid expands into new products, customer segments, and regulated use cases.

Responsibilities

- Review prospective and existing customer deals for regulatory, licensing, policy risk, with a focus on the customer's business model, use case, product configuration, geography, and regulated activities.

- Conduct onboarding and enhanced diligence for higher-risk customers or use cases, including gathering and evaluating relevant licenses, registrations, policies, ownership information, and other supporting documentation.

- Partner with Sales, Account Management, Legal, Product, Risk Operations, and other stakeholders to identify compliance requirements, resolve open questions, and develop practical risk mitigations or approval conditions.

- Document compliance decisions, rationale, conditions, and escalations in a clear and auditable manner.

- Track open onboarding conditions, approvals, renewals, and other post-deal compliance obligations to ensure timely follow-through.

- Support reviews of regulated or higher-risk segments, including gaming and other industries where licensing or jurisdiction-specific requirements may apply.

- Research and interpret regulatory and licensing requirements relevant to customer activities, products, and markets, escalating novel or complex issues to subject-matter experts as appropriate.

- Develop and maintain GTM compliance playbooks, risk-tiering frameworks, decision trees, intake requirements, and escalation paths.

- Identify recurring deal or onboarding issues and partner with cross-functional teams to improve policies, controls, tooling, training, and customer-facing guidance.

- Provide training and office-hours support to GTM teams so they understand when to engage Compliance and how to gather the information needed for efficient reviews.

- Build reporting and metrics on review volume, turnaround times, risk themes, escalations, and outcomes to help Compliance and GTM leadership identify trends and prioritize improvements.

Qualifications

- 4-6 years of experience in Compliance, Legal, Risk, Operations, or a related function, preferably in fintech, financial services, payments, te

description:

About TCP (TimeClock Plus)
For more than 30 years, TCP has helped organizations engage their people by providing flexible, mobile timekeeping and workforce management solutions. Trusted by tens of thousands of customers and millions of users, TCP delivers proven technology and personalized support to organizations of all sizes in the public and private sector to meet their complex timekeeping, employee scheduling, leave management and other workforce needs. We recently embraced our refreshed brand, and completed our acquisition of Humanity Schedule, a cloud-based scheduling platform. Growth is happening and our vision for the future is clear. We'd love you to join us on this journey. For more information, visit or follow us on LinkedIn or Facebook.
The Role
As a Mid-Market Account Executive, SLED, you'll be responsible for driving and closing business, generating new leads and managing your growing pipeline. You will be the face of TCP to your customers and prospects and act as their main point of contact through the full sales cycle. We are looking for candidates with a "hunter" mentality, a drive to succeed and grow professionally, and a positive, self-starting mindset. If you have 3-5 years of successful SaaS sales experience and crushed both your rookie year and your fully ramped year, we would love to chat with you.
What You'll Do

• Serve as a subject matter expert and advisor to prospective customers through knowledge of current trends and topics within your assigned market segment.

• Develop and execute a strategic territory plan focused on State, Local Government, and Education (SLED) accounts, building relationships with key stakeholders and driving net-new business.

• Navigate complex SLED procurement processes, including RFPs, cooperative purchasing agreements, and budget cycles, to position and close workforce management solutions.

• Use a consultative approach to uncover workforce management challenges within SLED organizations and match them to solutions that deliver measurable results.

• Drive recurring subscription revenue through new customers.

• Achieve and exceed your assigned sales revenue quota.

• Conduct needs assessments across multiple customer groups, including technical, line-of-business, and executive stakeholders.

• Communicate the features and benefits of our software products clearly.

• Maintain an organized database of accounts, opportunities, and associated activities.

• Deliver customized presentations and product demonstrations.

• Manage, track, and accurately forecast revenue opportunities.

• Communicate a compelling, concise value proposition to potential customers.

• Promote TCP and its capabilities to your assigned market segments.

• Focus on prospecting and outbound sales generation.

• Complete a minimum of 25 prospecting calls per day. This is a daily minimum, not a weekly average.

• Maintain a sales mix of 80% self-generated business, 10% marketing and inbound leads, and 10% partnerships.

• Own territory planning and management.

• Travel 20-30%.
Requirements
• Bachelor's degree preferred.

• 3-5 years of experience selling SaaS and running the full sales cycle, from initial outreach to a completed agreement.

• Track record of building pipeline at 3-5x quota.

• Ability to create and assess sales opportunities through a consultative approach.

title: Data Science, Metrics
description:

title: Office and Event Manager
description:
CONTEXT

Hexa is looking for its new Office & Event Manager, for our offices at 12 rue Martel, Paris 10e. Our current office manager is moving on after some great years here.

The place is La Cristallerie: 800 m² under a glass roof, twelve meeting rooms, an atrium that seats 80, a professional kitchen and a three-camera podcast studio. Around 150 people work here every day, between our core team, the 12 companies we build each year, the 60 in our portfolio and our subtenants.

WHY THE ROLE EXISTS

No two weeks in this building look alike. 😄 A company arrives as a team of two and leaves as fifteen. A founder flies in from Berlin for 48 hours and needs a desk, a room and a coffee that does not taste like an airport. Event for 100 on Tuesday, podcast shoot Wednesday, masterclass Thursday morning with the atrium reset by 9am.

We are looking for the person who holds all of that together: the walls and the vendors, and the atmosphere too. Someone who knows the first name of everyone who walks through the door, who knows which team arrived on Monday and still needs introducing, who notices the startup keeping to itself in the corner and goes to get them.

THE TEAM

You would report to Camille, VP People & Community. And work in a team of six: Laure on Talent Acquisition, Juliette on HR Ops, Paul as Talent Engineer and Faustine as Head of Community. A small team, a wide scope, and people who genuinely enjoy working together.

MISSIONS

Run the building:

- Own the vendor relationships (cleaning, maintenance, security, caterers, suppliers): choose them, negotiate them, hold them to their word.

- Own the venue budget end to end, trade-offs included.

- Manage the space itself: floor plan, teams moving in and out, room bookings, and the diplomacy of four people wanting the atrium on the same Thursday.

- Handle whatever the building throws at you, from the leak to the AC giving up on conference day, through to resolution.

- Keep the podcast studio alive: bookings, setup, guest welcome, gear in working order.

Animate the workplace:

- Be the face of the place, the person people come to for everything and the one who already anticipated half of it.

- Onboard incoming teams: the tour, the house rules, introductions to their new neighbours, the small fixes of week one.

- Engineer the encounters, like a lunch that seats two founders together because you noticed they were solving the same problem.

- Read the temperature of the building and flag what is wrong before it reaches us on its own.

Produce the events:

- Breakfasts, masterclasses, demo days, dinners, parties, offsites, farewells, birthdays. The build-up (budget, vendors, logistics, run of show) and the day itself (setup, coordination, being in the room, breakdown).

- Host our startups' and subtenants' own events too, and make sure they leave wanting the date back next quarter.

Look after the core team:

- The office management essentials for 40 people: orders, mail, welcome packs, equipment, the small daily emergencies.

- Plus support to the HR team on people experience for Hexa employees: offsites, team retreats, demo times.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

You have run a venue, with clients inside it and vendors around it. Probably from hospitality (operations manager, duty manager, head concierge, meetings & events manager), from events (venue manager, production coordinator, stage or technical manager), or from managed offices, coworking, campuses and incubators.

- You can handle a budget and negotiate without turning it into a standoff.

- The extra mile is a reflex. You go and buy the flowers yourself because the florist sent something sad, and you stay twenty minutes longer because the evening is going well.

- You like people, and it shows without you having to work at it.

- The unexpected energizes you rather than tightening you up. A leak never gives notice, and neither does a founder.

- Working French and English. The building is bilingual.

ONE THING WE WOULD RATHER

title: Solutions Architect

Push the boundaries of tech. In your sweatpants.

•
We want you to be you . Too often, companies tell you about their culture and then expect you to fit it. Our culture is built from the people who work here. We want you to feel safe to be who you are, take risks, and show us what you’ve got.

•
It’s your world. We know you have a life. We want to be part of it, but not all of it. At Parallels , we’re serious about empowering people to work when, how, and where they want. Couch? Sweatpants? • Develop and own migration guides covering MDM enrollment, Windows image creation and delivery, app compatibility validation, and identity/SSO integration

• Support customer-specific edge cases, like non-standard app stacks, regulated industries, air-gapped environments, complex RBAC requirements

Lab, Tooling & Experimentation

• Maintain a live, current lab environment that mirrors real enterprise conditions across macOS versions, Parallels releases, and management platforms

title: AI Cinematographer - Buenos Aires
description:
Noë & Associates is a global brand consultancy working across real estate, hospitality, and luxury. We specialise in the unbuilt - creating brands and telling the stories of places before they exist. From our studios in New York, London, and Dubai, we have helped bring billions of dollars of developments to market for clients including Aman, Rosewood, Mandarin Oriental, Jumeirah, and IHG. We are hiring an AI Cinematographer to help us picture the unbuilt: cinematic film and motion, made with the new generation of generative video tools, for some of the world’s most ambitious luxury developments and destinations. We are proud to be part of Together Group , a curated collective of high-quality creative consultancies, marketing, technology and production studios. Together, we create and elevate brands, experiences and destinations of the future.

This role is initially offered on a contract basis, with the potential to become permanent.

Key Responsibilities

The role

This is a craft role at the frontier. You trained in film and you think like a cinematographer - in composition, lens, light, movement, and pace - and you have carried that language into AI video, where the tools now let us show a place, a feeling, and a way of living long before anything is built. You will work alongside our strategists, designers, editors, and producers to develop the look and feel of residences, resorts, and destinations still in design - turning a vision into something a client and their audience can actually see and feel.

What you’ll do

• Create cinematic film and motion with generative video tools - from early concept films to finished campaign work. • Work primarily in Kling, our current tool of choice, with room to use Seedance and other tools where they serve the work better. • Translate real cinematographic craft - framing, lensing, lighting, camera movement, edit rhythm - into prompts, references, and generative workflows that hold a high bar for taste and finish. • Develop looks and visual worlds for the unbuilt: places that do not yet exist, made convincing and beautiful on screen. • Exercise judgement about tools - which model or approach serves a given shot, and when a result is genuinely good enough to ship. • Stay at the edge of a fast-moving field and bring back what is worth using.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

• A real grounding in film. Film school or equivalent training, with genuine command of cinematic language, pacing, and storytelling - film specifically, not photography. You think in motion, and you know how a single shot lives within a sequence. • Fluency with AI video generation. Hands-on experience with Kling especially; Seedance and/or other generative tools are valued, along with the judgement to know which suits the shot. • An eye for the high end. Taste, precision, and restraint suited to luxury brands - with a feel for architecture and the spaces our work brings to life. • Self-direction. Clear communication and the discipline to own work across time zones.

We are open on level. The role suits a recent film graduate fluent in today’s tools, but we are glad to talk to stronger candidates.

title: Senior | Staff Software Engineer - AI / ML
description:
About Snorkel

At Snorkel, we believe meaningful AI doesn’t start with the model, it starts with the data.

We’re on a mission to help enterprises transform expert knowledge into specialized AI at scale. The AI landscape has gone through incredible changes since 2015, when Snorkel started as a research project in the Stanford AI Lab, to the generative AI breakthroughs of today. But one thing has remained constant: the data you use to build AI is the key to achieving differentiation, high performance, and production-ready systems. We work with some of the world’s largest organizations to empower scientists, engineers, financial experts, product creators, journalists, and more to build custom AI with their data faster than ever before. Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

In September 2026 we raised a $350 million Series E at a $3.5 billion valuation , and we are scaling our engineering and research teams to meet demand.

The role

Frontier AI data is expensive to make and hard to measure. Every task we deliver is tested against the strongest models, often through many long-running agent rollouts. Your job is to make that process faster, cheaper, and more rigorous with ML and AI

You will be one of the early members of ML & Research Engineering at Snorkel. You will study how frontier-grade data is generated and evaluated, form hypotheses, validate them against real production data, and ship the winners at scale. You will shape the discipline's direction, its standards, and the team that grows around it.

What you'll work on

• Efficient agentic evals. Cut the cost of long-horizon agent evaluation with adaptive sampling, statistically grounded early stopping, model cascades, caching, and cheap-first gating.

• AI model routing. Route every eval and judge call to the cheapest model that clears the quality bar, with fallback, monitoring, and cost attribution.

• Fine-tuned small models. Fine-tune and serve open-weight models (LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods) where they match frontier quality, and know when they don't.

• Predictive difficulty. Build models that estimate how hard a task is for frontier systems before running a single rollout.

• Measurement for AI data. Build golden datasets, quantify the accuracy and calibration of LLM-as-judge systems, and make quality reproducible across projects.

• Research to production. Turn research prototypes into reusable, configurable components that forward deployed engineers and researchers use on every project.

What you'll bring

• 5+ years building production ML or software systems, with end-to-end ownership from prototype to production

• Hands-on experience running LLM or ML workloads in production, and comfort reasoning about non-deterministic systems

• Deep grounding in statistics and experimentation: experiment design, hypothesis testing, sampling, and confidence intervals

• Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals, including testing, code review, and system design

• Experience designing evaluations and interpreting results rigorously

• A habit of finding high-impact problems before they are assigned, and clear communication with researchers, engineers, and business partners

Nice to have

• Fine-tuning and serving open-weight models, and judging when a smaller model meets the quality bar

• Building LLM evaluation or experimentation platforms, model gateways, or routing systems

• Experience with agentic workloads, benchmarks, or RL environments

• A record of taking research into production: publications, open-source work, or shipped research-driven features

• MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a related field

Why join now

• Frontier problems. Measure and shape the tasks designed to challenge the strongest models in the world.

• All AI, no plumbing. Every problem on this team is an open ML or LLM problem.

• Founding impact. Help define what ML engineering means at Snorkel

title: Senior Trust & Safety Engineer
description:
Powering Great Work

We started as the place to find a trusted trade. Now, as we shape the future of home improvement, we're building the tech to transform that landscape for everyone - better products, smarter data, AI where it actually helps - so trades can spend less time on admin and consumers can find someone they trust, first time. That's Powering Great Work, and it's why every team here exists:

🔧 Trades spend less time on admin and more on winning work and growing their business

🏠 Homeowners get a trusted trade, first time, every time

🚀 We get to build products that change homes and lives across the country

As our next Senior Software Engineer in Trust & Safety, you'll own the systems that decide how tradespeople are checked, how reviews are processed and how our marketplace stays honest at scale. You'll work alongside the vetting and reviews teams, who are on the front line of trust, and build the infrastructure that lets them work with confidence. When something breaks in production, you'll lead the response. When something looks brittle at design time, you'll say so.

The job, unfiltered:

- Own and evolve the systems behind how tradespeople are verified, how reviews flow through our platform and how content is moderated.

- Lead the response when things break: read distributed traces, correlate logs across services and find the cause, not just the symptom.

- Design event-driven workflows that are reliable by default: idempotent, retryable, with dead-letter handling that doesn't need a 2am wake-up to unpick.

- Work directly with the vetting and reviews teams to understand what trust means day to day, then build systems that hold up to it.

- Tighten the operational seams: better monitoring, clearer alerting, locked-down auth and outbox patterns that keep data consistent.

The fit:

- Strong TypeScript. You're comfortable owning a service end to end, from schema to deployment.

- Fastify or a similar Node.js framework, and enough HTTP know-how that it rarely surprises you.

- Event-driven instincts: you know what idempotency means in practice and why the outbox pattern exists.

- Full-stack comfort, Next.js included. You ship the frontend as happily as the service behind it.

- Datadog fluency (APM traces, log search, metric queries), SQL for diagnostics during an incident, and GCP basics such as Pub/Sub backlogs and DLQs.

- Experience leading production incidents, not just being in them. You communicate clearly under pressure and drive to a fix.

- An eye for systemic problems at review time, not at post-mortem time, and a habit of making the people around you better.

- Regular use of AI tools like Cursor or Claude Code, and a keen interest in helping the team get more out of them.

You don't need to know our Trust & Safety domain yet (the review lifecycle, vetting disposition logic, publish timing). You'll pick it up. What matters is that you learn fast and take it seriously.

(Don't self-select out because you don't tick every box. We'd rather meet you.)

What you get

💰 Competitive salary, annual bonus & equity scheme

🩺 Health, wellbeing and learning support

🚲 Gym membership, Smart Tech Scheme, Cycle Scheme

🎂 Birthday/special day leave, buy & sell holiday scheme

❤️ 1 week's paid charity leave, and more

How this goes

- Screening call with one of our Talent Acquisition Partners

- Technical interview with members of the team

- Final stage with the hiring manager and a senior stakeholder

ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands - including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank - to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Run the monthly and quarterly commission cycle, from pulling data and calculating commissions to validating payouts, getting approvals and handing off to payroll.

- Investigate rep questions, document what you find, recommend fixes, and clear issues quickly so reps trust their payouts.

- Work with Salesforce and data owners to keep source data clean, map new fields and deal types, and find upstream problems before they turn into payout errors.

- Reconcile and audit payouts against payroll, bookings and plan terms every cycle.

- Model the cost and payout impact of proposed plan changes and set up new plans in the system.

- Automate manual steps, tighten SLAs and build reporting on attainment, payout cost and comp effectiveness.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

- 5+ years in sales compensation, commissions operations or a closely related finance/RevOps role.

- A track record of managing commission cycles across multiple regions, currencies, and payroll schedules, from data collection through payout validation, approvals, and payroll handoff.

- Strong analytical skills, including payout modeling, data reconciliation, and investigating discrepancies against compensation plan terms.

- Experience using Salesforce to pull and review sales data for commission calculations.

- Ability to configure sales compensation tools to calculate, validate, and report commission payouts.

- Clear, calm communication with sellers and leaders, including during difficult payout conversations.

EVEN BETTER…

- Familiarity with commission accounting, including accruals, journal entries, and month-end close.

OUR VALUES

- Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

- Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

- Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

- Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it.

description:

We make eco-friendly products and donate 50% of our profits to provide clean water and help build toilets for the billions of people who lack proper access. Over the next couple of years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold to get us closer to our dream of everyone in the world having access to clean water and sanitation services.

A bit about the role

As our Financial Accounting Manager, you’ll be the person who really knows what’s going on inside our UK numbers. You’ll own the monthly close for our UK balance sheet, get across our transaction flows and revenue channels, and work closely with our UK commercial team to keep things on track. You’ll also lead one of our more exciting projects this year: building a proper playbook for how we onboard big new retail customers, so every new partnership starts on the right foot. title: Structural Engineer
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

ROLE SCOPE

- Engineer the structures: modular units, equipment supports, and buildings designed for fast fabrication and faster erection.

title: Venture Scout
description:
We are hiring a Venture Scout to find companies worth our diligence, and to open relationships with investors who back private companies directly.

Pairs is a global network of family offices, institutional investors, VCs and angels. We screen deal flow very tightly, and the opportunities that clear our diligence go out to the network. We invest alongside them too.

THE ROLE
This role works across both sides of Pairs. It is for people who bring in deals on their own. You bring founders from your own network who are raising, learn what makes their companies worth an investor's time, and bring the strongest to Pairs.

Most of the work is first contact done well. You write to founders and investors in a way that earns a reply, turn those replies into calls, and bring the right ones into the network.

We are not raising a fund. Our investors invest directly in companies, so the work is about direct investors, not fund LPs.

Our platform handles the pipeline, research and follow-up. Your time goes to the conversations, and to learning which companies and investors are ready.

You will work directly with the two co-founders and our investor team, on a process that already works. The organisation is flat, so you will see first-hand how we screen opportunities, what we decline and why.

This is an early-career role. Drive and judgement matter more to us than years in a seat.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

- Company sourcing. Founders raising Series A and later, found early and brought to Pairs with the context our team needs.

- First conversations. Messages that read like a person wrote them, and replies turned into calls.

- Investor research. Who is investing right now, in what, at what stage and cheque size.

- Your growing network. Every founder and investor you open, kept current and qualified. The network you build here is yours.

YOU ARE A FIT IF YOU

- Already have an active network of founders you can bring to the table, built through an accelerator, a VC role, a startup community or your own work.

- Can write a short, specific message to a stranger that gets a reply.

- Keep your pace high without letting quality slip, and follow a process without needing a reminder.

- Understand the basics of a round: stage, cheque size, SAFE versus priced, and why an investor passes.

- Treat discretion as second nature. Please do not include any investor or company names in your application.

- Use AI tools daily, with clear judgement about where they improve your work and where they would compromise its quality.

WHAT WE OFFER

- A fully remote, asynchronous role

- Direct access to the co-founders and our investor team

- Close collaboration with our internal team

- Live mandates from your first week, and access to the opportunities that clear our diligence

- Insight into our internal processes, including how we screen deal flow

- Room to grow into a Venture Partner role as your network grows

- A base salary plus commission
